newsitem.title: ALGERIA: Algeria's FFS to take part in the polls.
newsitem.headline: Algeria's FFS to take part in the polls.

text.p: Algeria's main secular opposition party, the Socialist Forces Front (FFS), said on Thursday it would take part in the June 5 parliamentary election.

Party leader Seddik Debaili said the FFS had been wary of taking part in the polls because it did not believe the vote would stop the fighting between the security forces and Islamist militants. About 60,000 people have been killed in the conflict.

The FFS advocates dialogue to end the civil strife that broke out in 1992 after authorities cancelled a general election in which radical Islamists had taken a commanding lead. Algeria has been without an elected parliament since then.
The Algerian government rejects dialogue with the militant Islamists.

"The choice was very difficult for us because if we participate in the elections without a clear goal to restore peace that means reneging on the party policy and if we boycott the poll we risk marginalising the party in the political field," Debaili told Reuters.

"Everybody believes that the elections will not end the violence. With the elections, the violence will continue and most people do not believe that the elections would be a solution to the crisis," he said.
But members urged the party to avoid "making a show of non-attendance", he said.
About 30 political parties are expected to field about 4,000 candidates in the elections of the 380-seat National Assembly, political sources said.
